author: francisdb
body:
## Summary

Follow-up to #308. Moves the BufWriter/BufReader policy out of every call site and into the `FileSystem` trait, where each impl can answer for itself whether extra buffering is warranted.

- Adds default methods `FileSystem::create_buffered_file` and `open_buffered_file`. Defaults wrap `create_file` / `open_file` in `BufWriter` / `BufReader`.
- `MemoryFileSystem` overrides both to delegate to the raw methods - its writer is `Vec<u8>`-backed and its reader is a `Cursor<Vec<u8>>`, both already byte-buffered. The extra layer was harmless but pointless.
- Collapses the call-site plumbing introduced in #308 (`BufWriter::new(fs.create_file(...))` -> `fs.create_buffered_file(...)`).

## Read side too

While at it, this PR fixes the symmetric read-side gap that #308 didn't touch:

- `src/vpx/expanded/util.rs::read_json` (the central JSON reader used by sounds, fonts, info, gamedata, collections, renderprobes, gameitems, images) now uses `open_buffered_file`.
- The three direct `open_file` + `serde_json::from_reader` sites in `src/vpx/expanded/materials.rs` (current, legacy, legacy-physics) too.

That gives the same NAS-friendly behaviour on read that #308 gave on write. `serde_json::from_reader` issues many small reads per token; unbuffered on a network mount is slow for the same reasons unbuffered writes were.

## Out of scope (still)

- `read_obj_from_reader<R: BufRead>` already requires `BufRead` at the type level, and all callers wrap in `BufReader` before calling.
- `read_glb_from_reader` is called on `Cursor<Vec<u8>>`, in-memory.
- CompoundFile (`cfb`) reads/writes - the trait requires `Read + Write + Seek`, so external buffering wouldn't fit.

## Notes

- Public API addition only: existing `create_file` / `open_file` callers (none in this PR, but downstream) keep working unchanged.
- `flush()?` is still called explicitly at write sites. `Drop`-time flush errors are swallowed regardless of how the writer was constructed - there's no way around that without a typed wrapper, which would defeat the `dyn Write` erasure.

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo build` - clean
- [x] `cargo clippy --all-targets` - clean
- [x] `cargo test --lib` - all 354 tests pass

## Summary
Mobile job page did three sequential network roundtrips before the page could render:
1. /api/auth?action=me
2. /api/jobs?id=X (inside bootstrapAuth)
3. /api/data (inside load())

All three only need JOB_ID which is known at script-eval time. Pre-fire all three at module scope so they race. bootstrapAuth and load() consume the already-flying promises when their await comes due.

## Impact
Saves ~one network roundtrip on cold loads. Most noticeable on flaky mobile signal where each roundtrip can be 200-500ms.

## Worst case
Logged-out user: all three 401, auth catch redirects to /login. One speculative job + data fetch wasted per logged-out load. Cheap.

## Test plan
- [ ] /jobs/:id loads correctly for tradies, LH, admin, clients
- [ ] Expired-session user still redirects to /login
- [ ] No regression on offline-aware BuhlQueue paths
- [ ] No console errors

author: meharsg96
body:
## Summary

Adds `jstests/aggregation/sources/merge/concurrent_replay_idempotency.js` (~158 lines) pinning the documented idempotency property of `$merge`: running the same deterministic aggregation pipeline twice against the same unchanged source must produce the same target-collection state.

Three sub-tests, one per `whenMatched` mode that touches existing rows: `replace`, `merge`, `keepExisting` (each paired with `whenNotMatched: "insert"`). Each:

1. Drops + recreates a deterministic 1000-event source collection.
2. Drops + recreates a target collection.
3. Runs the same `$group → $merge` pipeline twice.
4. Asserts `orderedArrayEq(snap1, snap2)` AND `fingerprint1 === fingerprint2`.

This invariant is load-bearing for materialized-view rematerialization and exactly-once stream-processing patterns built on top of `$merge`.

**Jira:** https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/SERVER-126534

## Files

- `jstests/aggregation/sources/merge/concurrent_replay_idempotency.js`

No source changes; no helpers changed. Imports match neighboring tests in this directory (`dropWithoutImplicitRecreate` from `merge_helpers.js`, `orderedArrayEq` from `utils.js`).

## What this catches

A future patch that breaks `$merge`'s bit-identical replay — `whenMatched` semantics regression, upsert misordering under concurrent shard targets, or nondeterministic `_id` generation on a replay codepath — will fail one of the two assertions per mode.

## Verify

Syntax-check parity with a neighbor test:

```
node --input-type=module --check jstests/aggregation/sources/merge/concurrent_replay_idempotency.js
```

Run under resmoke against an unsharded mongod (standard aggregation suite invocation).

## Related

- SERVER-99827 explicitly excludes `$merge` tests from config-transition suites due to unsafe retries. The invariant pinned here is the structural property that has to hold before any of those exclusions can be safely reverted. This PR is a step toward that, not a fix for SERVER-99827.

## Draft status

Opened as Draft. Test is green-only (no counterexample mode); please retarget the component label if Aggregation Framework is not the right reviewer group.

`ArrayRef` is a non-owning view and does not store the underlying data. Initializing it with {64, 64} creates a temporary array whose lifetime ends at the end of the full expression, resulting in a dangling reference. author: genisis0x
body:
## Summary

`FilesystemToolkit` exposes `read_file`, `write_file`, and `update_file` tools that the model uses to manipulate user files on disk. All three called `Path.read_text()` / `Path.write_text()` without an explicit encoding, so each operation inherited `locale.getpreferredencoding()` — `cp1252` on most Windows installs:

- `read_file` raised `UnicodeDecodeError` on any file whose bytes weren't valid cp1252 (most modern source files, JSON / YAML with non-ASCII strings, Markdown with smart quotes, anything with emoji or CJK glyphs).
- `write_file` raised `UnicodeEncodeError` on any payload the model generated that wasn't representable in cp1252 (the same set of characters).
- `update_file` did the read and the write in the same call against the platform default, so a round-trip on Windows silently transcoded the file every time the model edited it.

Same class of bug as #1731 / #2814 / #2815, this time on the LLM-facing beta toolkit.

## Fix

Pass `encoding=\"utf-8\"` explicitly at all three call sites so the toolkit produces the same bytes on Linux, macOS, and Windows. No change to the public tool signatures; no new options. Inline comments explain why the kwarg is required so a future refactor doesn't drop it again.

## Test

`test/beta/tools/test_filesystem.py` gets three regression tests that drive the toolkit through `Agent.ask` (per `test/beta/CLAUDE.md`'s public-API guidance) and assert byte-level equality against the explicit UTF-8 encoding of the payload — not against `Path.read_text()`, which would mask the bug on POSIX:

- `test_write_file_encodes_as_utf8`
- `test_read_file_decodes_as_utf8`
- `test_update_file_preserves_utf8` — replaces an ASCII token with a CJK glyph so the read+write pair has to round-trip non-cp1252 content.

`npm test` equivalent: `.venv/bin/python -m pytest test/beta/tools/test_filesystem.py` reports 16 passed.

body:
## Summary

Second Phase 3b PR. Builds on Phase 3b.1 (#1259, merged) by registering AnthropicProvider unconditionally and routing the per-verb gating + the threshold-violation expiry-extraction through the registry. After this lands, Phase 3b.2 plugs Google in as a second registry entry.

## Honest scope

The Anthropic refresh exchange continues to flow through \`account-refresh.ts:refreshAccountIfNeeded\` directly (not through \`provider.refresh()\`). Anthropic's refresh has been load-bearing through RFC H's review and is tightly coupled with the broker's storage layer; routing it through a uniform interface adds indirection without value.

What the provider interface contributes today:
- \`extractExpiresAt(creds)\` — used in the broker's threshold-violation check. Replaces hardcoded \`creds?.claudeAiOauth?.expiresAt\` access. **Phase 3b.2's Google provider's \`extractExpiresAt\` returns \`googleOauth.expiresAt\` and the same code path works.**
- \`validateCredentialShape(creds)\` — used at \`add-account\` time, replacing hardcoded \`"claudeAiOauth" in req.credentials\` check.
- Registry presence — \`registry.has(provider)\` gates incoming requests; \`registry.names()\` powers the operator-actionable error message.

The AccountKey state-keying refactor (the bigger piece) is **deliberately deferred to Phase 3b.2** when Google actually has its own state to put alongside Anthropic's. See the v3 spec §7 Phase 3b decomposition for the rationale — the abstraction is at the dispatch layer where 3b.2 needs it, not the state layer that Anthropic-only-as-currently-shaped is fine for.

## What ships

- \`src/auth/broker/anthropic-provider.ts\` (new, ~95 LOC) — implements Provider interface; \`refresh()\` returns honest "use the direct path" error.
- \`src/auth/broker/server.ts\` — adds \`providers: ProviderRegistry\` field; refactors all four provider-aware verb dispatchers to use \`registry.has()\` for gating, \`provider.validateCredentialShape\` for cross-check; routes threshold-violation expiry-extraction through \`providers.lookup("anthropic").extractExpiresAt()\`.

- 78 pre-existing tests still pass (no regressions)
- 3 server tests updated to match new error messages ("not registered (only anthropic available)" replaces "Phase 3b.1b deferral")
- 1 new "regression-resistant" test pins the rejection message **shape** (\`/only .*anthropic.* available/\`) so Phase 3b.2 can update it by adding "google" without rewriting the assertion
- Existing back-compat test (add-account-without-provider-field) still passes

body:
## Summary
- Fingerprint job now resolves the plugin SHA and emits two hashes: `backend-hash` (gates pure-backend jobs) and `e2e-hash` = sha256(backend-hash + plugin-sha) (gates `e2e-clerk`).
- `e2e-clerk` checks out plugin at the exact `PLUGIN_SHA` from the fingerprint job, eliminating drift between cache key and tested code.
- `record-pass` saves both markers; `deploy-fastraid` requires either `ci` success or BOTH cache hits.
- New `report-cached-pass-to-plugin` job posts cached green to plugin commits when `e2e-clerk` is skipped on dispatch.

## Why
Plugin PR re-dispatches against an unchanged backend tree previously hit the backend-only cache and skipped `e2e-clerk` → plugin PR got a false green. Symmetrically, backend pushes with the plugin main branch moved would also skip e2e against the new plugin code. The split-hash fingerprint makes the cache key mean what it should: "this exact (backend, plugin) pair has been validated."

(Reopened from #134 — original branch name `ci/...` was not in the push-trigger allow-list so CI never started.)

## Test plan
- [ ] First push: backend + e2e caches both miss → full suite runs and seeds both markers
- [ ] Re-push same content: both cache hits → `ci` skips
- [ ] Dispatch from plugin PR with new plugin SHA: e2e miss → `e2e-clerk` runs, posts status
- [ ] Dispatch with unchanged plugin SHA after green: e2e hit → `e2e-clerk` skips, `report-cached-pass-to-plugin` posts success
- [ ] Backend push with plugin main moved: e2e miss but backend hit → only `e2e-clerk` re-runs

issue #107 で判明した LRU bench の構造的ミスマッチを修正し、公式 MAB 準拠の summarization eval に作り直した上で、bench 実機の反復観測でスコアを改善した。

**結果: LRU pass 0/8 → 3/8、mean F1 0.016 → 0.449**(CI sample 8 rows)

## 構造修正(issue #107 本体)

公式 MAB の `Long_Range_Understanding` split 110 rows を実データ調査した結果:
- `infbench_sum` 100 rows(本まるごとの要約タスク、`metadata.keypoints` 6-48個付き)+ `detective_qa` 10 rows(別タスク)
- 公式 `summarization_evaluate.py` は recall を dataset の `keypoints` に対し**列挙形式**で算出

旧実装のバグ: 要約指示文に BM25 retrieval → top-10 chunk (~10K字) を全編 reference と照合 → 原理的に一致しない。

- **`run_lru_summarization`** 新設: retrieval cascade をバイパス
- LRU split を `infbench_sum` 100 行のみに filter(detective_qa は follow-up #108)
- recall を公式準拠に: dataset の `metadata.keypoints` を ground truth に

## スコア改善の反復(bench 実機観測ベース)

| iteration | 内容 | mean F1 |
|---|---|---|
| v1 | count-based judge、ExtractiveBM25 multi-pass 凝縮 | 0.016 |
| v2 | **multi-signal extractive 凝縮**(centroid + MMR + proper-noun density + position、研究準拠の non-LLM 抽出) | 0.130 |
| v3-4 | summarizer prompt(固有名詞そのまま使用 / 三人称 / 全体弧)+ recall judge を公式準拠の**列挙形式** `{"supported_key_points": [...], "recall": N}` に | recall 改善 |
| v5 | precision judge も列挙形式 `{"supported_sentences": [...], "precision": N}` に | precision 一部改善 |
| **v6** | recall/precision judge を **`reasoning_effort: "high"` + max_tokens 8192** に(列挙照合は重く low では judge が空リストで諦める) | **0.449 (3/8 pass)** |

判明した主な失敗モードと対策:
- **一人称小説で主人公が無名化** → summarizer prompt で「三人称・語り手名を本文から特定」
- **古典小説の正規名置換**(Victor↔擬名 Kiran)→ prompt で「ソースの固有名詞をそのまま使う」
- **extractive 凝縮の情報損失**(語彙中心性のみ・主人公名脱落)→ multi-signal 抽出
- **recall/precision judge が bare count だと 0 に倒れる** → 公式準拠の index 列挙形式
- **列挙照合が reasoning budget 不足で空リスト** → high reasoning_effort

`CaseDiagnostic` に `keypoints` を追加し recall 採点のデバッグを可能にした。

## 残課題(#91 の judge 品質の壁)

3票アンサンブルの vote ばらつき(row0 recall: 14 vs 33)、precision の過大評価傾向(mean 0.89)が残る。これは issue #91 が指摘した「現 judge は fine-grained 判定が不安定 → GPT-4o 級 judge が必要」の領域で、reasoning budget 引き上げが現 judge での実質的な上限。

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo test -p tsumugi-bench` (184 passed) — condense / 列挙形式 parser / infbench filter / 各 helper のテストを追加
- [x] `cargo fmt --check` / `cargo clippy -p tsumugi-bench --all-targets` clean
- [x] bench 実機で 6 イテレーション観測(最新 run 25853562239: LRU 3/8 pass、mean F1 0.449)。bench check は全 iteration で success(compare_snapshot は LRU pipeline 変更で legitimately 変わるが tolerance 内 / case_id shuffle のため)

## Follow-up

- #108: detective_qa 10 行を QA accuracy path で評価
- #91: GPT-4o 級 judge 入手後の LRU judge 安定化(vote ばらつき・precision 較正)

Implemented the initial authentication system for Axon using Django REST Framework. Added a custom user model with support for email verification, profile completion status, social profile links, and future OAuth integration support.

Built the user registration flow with serializer-based validation for unique email and username handling. Added secure password hashing using Django’s built-in authentication system.

Implemented secure email verification using cryptographically generated tokens with SHA256 hashing before database storage. Added token expiration handling and email verification workflow using Resend for transactional email delivery.

Created verification routes that validate hashed tokens, activate user accounts, clear verification fields after successful verification, and issue JWT authentication tokens using SimpleJWT.

Structured the backend with reusable email utilities and separated HTML email templates for future scalability, including onboarding emails, notifications, and password recovery systems.

The authentication flow now supports:

* Secure user registration
* Email verification
* JWT token generation
* Backend-controlled verification redirects
* Foundation for onboarding/profile completion flow
* Future support for Google and GitHub OAuth account linking

body:
Closes #269

## Changes

- **`web/src/App.tsx`**: Added a `feedQuery` using `useQuery` that calls `fetchFeed({ limit: 200 })` with `refetchInterval: 5000`. The `events` prop passed to `<TopBar>` is now derived from `feedQuery.data` (mapping `created_at` → `ts` epoch ms) instead of `activeQuery.data`. The `online` flag still comes from `activeQuery.isError` (connectivity semantics unchanged).
- **`web/src/lib/api.ts`**: Added `limit?: number` to `FeedParams` and wired it into the query string so the limit is forwarded to `/api/feed`.

The root cause was that `activeQuery` hits `/api/active` (currently running workers), which returns an empty array when no workers are active — so the TopBar rate was always 0. The feed endpoint returns timestamped historical events, which TopBar's existing `eventsLastMin` filter uses to compute the rolling 60s rate.

## Test Plan
- Start the dev server with recent feed events; TopBar should show a non-zero `N/min` count within 5s.
- When all feed events are older than 60s (or feed is empty), TopBar displays `0/min`.
- `npm run typecheck` and `npm run build` both pass.

body:
## Summary

Two changes that together would have made the **2026-05-14 `create_lastmile_order` HTTP 422 bug** self-diagnosing instead of opaque.

1. **`lib/tools/register.ts`** — centralized `registerTool` wrapper now catches `QuiqupHttpError` from any tool handler and returns a tool-result with `isError: true` containing the full upstream body (truncated to 4KB) plus a status-specific hint. Before this, all 23 M3 thin pass-through tools surfaced only `"Quiqup 422"` to the LLM; the actual rejection body (`attribute_errors[].detail`, etc.) was silently dropped.

2. **`lib/tools/whoami-platform.ts`** — new tool wrapping `GET https://platform-api.quiqup.com/me`. Returns `core_api_user_id`, `email`, `salesforce_id`, `region_code`, `roles`, and `admin/courier/csr` flags from the **exchanged** session-JWT. Disambiguates from `claims_dump` (which only decodes the **inbound** OAuth token, pre-exchange).

3. **`.github/workflows/claude-review.yml`** — bumped `--max-turns` 5 → 15 and tightened the prompt. The first real-content Claude Review run hit `error_max_turns` at the 5-turn cap before finishing.

## Why this PR instead of the obvious "fix the description"

The bug report listed 7 asks. Three of them (`update the tool description`, `share a working payload`, `pull platform-api log`) all depend on knowing the **actual** 422 rejection reason. The bug reporter never saw it because the MCP swallowed it. **Fixing the swallowing is the prerequisite** for everything else — once this lands, the next failing call returns the body and the description fix becomes mechanical.

## What's NOT in this PR

- **Updated `create_lastmile_order` description** — needs a real 422 body to know what field to add/fix. Once this PR lands, re-run the failing call, capture the body, and iterate in a follow-up.
- **Pull platform-api logs for the 5 captured request IDs** — no ops access from CI / Claude side. Becomes redundant once #1 surfaces the body to the caller directly.
- **Verify Clerk token exchange path** (bug-report hypothesis #6) — done as a read-only check; **disproven by the bug report's own data**. The user's pasted exchanged JWT shows `coreID: 464709` and `orgID: org_2ocjT...` ARE present. The "default" Clerk template is configured correctly; the MCP code calls `clerk.sessions.getToken(sessionId, "default")` and returns it unmodified. Not a bug.
- **Hypothesis #1 (unentitled partner)** — also disproven by `/me` returning `admin: true`, `region_code: "uae.dubai"`, and `partner_sameday` permission. The 422 is **payload-shape**, not auth.

## CI note

`Claude code review` reports failure on this PR for a known reason: **the action self-disables on any PR that modifies its own workflow file** (it validates that the workflow content on the PR matches the version on main exactly, to prevent secret-exfiltration via workflow edits). My commit `693378c` tweaks `--max-turns` from 5 to 15 + simplifies the prompt — that's what triggers the skip. The first run on this PR (commit `3b3d29f`, before the prompt tweak) actually fired and hit `error_max_turns` mid-review — that's what motivated the tweak.

Post-merge, subsequent PRs will:
- Pick up the improved prompt + 15-turn cap from main
- Pass Claude Review normally (assuming they don't modify the workflow themselves)

`Evals` workflow doesn't fire because none of the changed files (`lib/tools/register.ts`, `lib/tools/whoami-platform.ts`, `app/[transport]/route.ts`) are in its path filter. Neither eval (offline v1 or online v3) exercises the `registerTool` wrapper anyway — they call Anthropic / Quiqup directly — so the absence of an automated check here is correct, not a gap.

## Test plan

- [x] Local: `bun run test` → 41 passed + 1 skipped (unchanged)
- [x] Local: `bunx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json` → clean
- [ ] Manual repro after merge: ping the deployed MCP at `https://quiqup-mcp.vercel.app/mcp` with the Variant 5 minimal payload from the bug report. Expect a tool-result with `isError: true` containing the actual Quiqup 422 body — paste it in a follow-up so the description fix lands cleanly.
- [ ] Manual after merge: call new `whoami_platform` tool, confirm it returns the same `/me` shape the bug report pasted manually.

## Verification of bug-report hypotheses

| # | Hypothesis | Status |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | User → partner mapping missing / unentitled | **Disproven** — `/me` shows admin partner with `partner_sameday` |
| 2 | Address validation rules undocumented | Still possible; need real 422 body to confirm |
| 3 | Phone format strictly E.164 without `+` | Still possible |
| 4 | Items require `value`+`currency` for COD eligibility | Still possible |
| 5 | Service-lane edge case | Still possible |
| 6 | MCP token exchange drops `coreID`/`orgID` | **Disproven by bug report's own JWT paste** |

Hypotheses 2–5 will be answerable from the actual 422 body once this PR ships.

## Summary

Migrates the `RemoveGroupUser` RPC handler off `groupService.RemoveUsers` and onto a new `membershipService.RemoveGroupMember`, mirroring the add-side work in #1608. Proto RPC unchanged.

The new method enforces the min-owner constraint via the existing `DeleteWithMinRoleGuard` atomic pattern (same as `SetGroupMemberRole`). This replaces the handler-level pre-check that compared owner counts via `userService.ListByGroup` — that two-step had the same TOCTOU pattern fixed for org in #1590.

## Behavior

- User-facing behavior of `RemoveGroupUser` unchanged: same error code (`InvalidArgument` + `ErrGroupMinOwnerCount`) on last-owner attempts.
- Audit emits a new `GroupMemberRemovedEvent` audit record + context auditor log.
- `RemoveGroupMember` restricts principal types to `app/user` for now; the switch is extensible for future types (same convention as `SetGroupMemberRole`).

## What's intentionally not deleted

`groupService.RemoveUsers` / `removeUsers` stay. They serve the user-cascade path (`core/deleter` + `group.Delete`), which must bypass the min-owner constraint when the user is being destroyed system-wide. Matches the org pattern where `org.Service.RemoveUsers` and `membership.RemoveOrganizationMember` coexist.

- [x] `go test ./core/membership/... ./internal/api/v1beta1connect/...`

Project deletion required entering each project’s settings modal, which made multi-project cleanup slow. This change adds a lightweight selection workflow on the Projects listing to support single and multi-delete without redesigning the page or duplicating delete logic.

- **Projects list UX (minimal surface change)**
  - Added a `Select`/`Manage` mode on the Dashboard Projects section.
  - In selection mode, cards become selectable (instead of navigational), show selected state, and preserve existing card layout in normal mode.
  - Added compact toolbar with selected count, `Delete selected`, and `Cancel`.

- **Bulk delete flow**
  - Reused existing `deleteProject(projectId)` server action for each selected project.
  - Added confirmation step before delete execution, matching current deletion safety pattern.
  - Supports single and multi-select in the same flow.

- **State + consistency**
  - Implemented with local component state only (no global store changes).
  - Removed successfully deleted cards immediately from local list for instant feedback.
  - Triggered route refresh after delete completion to ensure dashboard/project counts and listing data are not stale.

- **Deletion safety and cascade behavior**
  - Kept existing server-side deletion path and Prisma cascade semantics intact (project → board/tasks/comments/members cleanup remains unchanged via current relations and `onDelete` behavior).

## Summary

Two related improvements that unblock running the `e2e-test-nfs-v3-full-sync` skill (and other e2e skills sharing `harness-run`) in lab environments that have:

1. **HTTP Basic Auth in front of ClickHouse** (e.g. a k8s-hosted cluster behind ingress)
2. **Non-UTF-8 system locales** on the runner (notably Windows GBK / Chinese)

Default single-node no-auth setups behave unchanged: empty `CLICKHOUSE_PASSWORD` means no Auth header is added.

## What changed

- `harness-run/scripts/env.py` — open `.env` with explicit `encoding="utf-8"`
- `harness-run/scripts/assertions.py` — `TerrasyncAssertions(ch_user=, ch_password=)`, Basic Auth header on both query/execute; all subprocess calls now `encoding="utf-8", errors="replace"`
- `e2e-test-nfs-v3-full-sync/scripts/run.py` — UTF-8 stdout/stderr reconfigure; thread CH creds into the assertion helper; propagate `CLICKHOUSE_HOST/USER/PASSWORD/NFS_EXPORT` into the remote `verify-metadata.sh` invocation via an SSH env prefix
- `e2e-test-nfs-v3-full-sync/scripts/verify-metadata.sh` — read `CLICKHOUSE_HOST`/`NFS_EXPORT` from env (default to existing `192.168.50.173:8123` / `/export/nfs`); attach `--user $USER:$PASSWORD` to `curl` when password is set
- `harness-run/.env.example` — add `CLICKHOUSE_USER` and `CLICKHOUSE_PASSWORD` placeholders with a "do not commit secrets" comment

## Test Plan

- [x] e2e ran end-to-end against an auth-protected 3-shard ClickHouse cluster on Windows (GBK locale), 527 entries verified
- [x] All defaults match prior single-node behavior — runs that don't set `CLICKHOUSE_USER`/`CLICKHOUSE_PASSWORD` send no Auth header
- [ ] Reviewer: smoke-test on a no-auth single-node CH to confirm backward compat in your environment

## Out of scope

This PR only touches the `nfs-v3-full-sync` skill's `run.py` for the env-prefix change. The other e2e skills don't currently call `verify-metadata.sh` with env-var-driven CH host, so they're untouched. Happy to fan out the same pattern to other skills in a follow-up if desired.

author: cdileep23
body:
Fix summary
Symptom: Production console showed CancelledError errors from two paths — the AG-Grid getRows catch in DevelopDataV2.jsx and the fire-and-forget refetchQueries in cacheUtils.js.

Root cause #1 — broken cancellation check (production-only)

React-query's CancelledError extends Error but the constructor never sets this.name → err.name === "Error", not "CancelledError".
The fallback err.constructor.name reads "CancelledError" in dev but gets minified to Xz in prod.
So the existing predicate name === "CancelledError" || ... always returned false in prod, and the cancellation leaked into logger.error("[getRows] failed", ...).
Root cause #2 — try/catch can't catch async rejections

try { queryClient.refetchQueries(...) } catch {} only catches synchronous throws. refetchQueries returns immediately with a pending Promise; the rejection lands on a later microtask, by which time the try block is gone → unhandled rejection.
Fix

Switched the react-query branch to isCancelledError(err) (imported from @tanstack/react-query). It's an instanceof CancelledError check, so it survives minification and doesn't depend on this.name. Axios CanceledError and AbortError already set name correctly, so those branches stayed as name checks.
Replaced the synchronous try/catch in cacheUtils.js with a swallowCancellations(label) handler attached via .catch(...) to each invalidate/refetchQueries call. Cancellations are silently dropped; real errors still log.

author: sroussey
body:
## Why

`WorkerServerBase.pendingAborts` previously used FIFO eviction at size 1000 (dropping the oldest 500 in bulk once the cap was crossed). A misbehaving client spamming aborts for ids that never landed could silently evict a legitimate pending abort before its matching `call` arrived — the run-fn would then execute un-aborted, defeating the whole abort-before-call race fix.

Separately, `runWithIterable`'s top JSDoc misleadingly suggested a two-way abort bond ("leaves the parent alone"). The implementation is actually parent → child only, and the wording invited future contributors to reintroduce reverse propagation by accident.

## What

**TTL-based pendingAborts** (`packages/util/src/worker/WorkerServerBase.ts`):
- `pendingAborts` is now `Map<string, number>` keyed on insertion timestamp instead of `Set<string>`.
- 30s TTL via `PENDING_ABORT_TTL_MS`. Each insertion schedules a one-shot `setTimeout` cleanup (mirrors the existing `scheduleCompletedRequestCleanup` pattern); timer handles are tracked in `pendingAbortTimers` so dispose-style hooks can clear them.
- Inline TTL sweep on every `recordPendingAbort` — drops any entries older than the TTL.
- 10k hard cap (`PENDING_ABORT_HARD_CAP`) as a memory safety-net; when exceeded, evict the half with the lowest timestamps (oldest-by-timestamp, not insertion order).
- `consumePendingAbort` rechecks the TTL on consumption: present + fresh → abort + delete + return `true`; present + expired → delete + return `false`; absent → return `false`.

**Comment fix** (`packages/ai/src/task/base/runWithIterable.ts`):
- Replace the misleading paragraph with explicit one-way-bond description plus two `@example` blocks showing parent-cancel vs consumer-break semantics.
- Add an inline `// One-way bond: parent -> child only.` marker above the `addEventListener("abort", ...)` line.

**Tests** (`packages/test/src/test/util/WorkerServerBase.race.test.ts`):
- New `describe("WorkerServerBase pendingAborts eviction policy", ...)` block with three cases under `vi.useFakeTimers()`:
  - **Eviction-correctness**: 1500 distinct aborts in a single tick + matching `call` for `a-500` → signal observed aborted (would have failed under FIFO).
  - **TTL-expiry**: single abort + `vi.advanceTimersByTime(31_000)` + matching `call` → signal observed un-aborted.
  - **Hard-cap safety**: `HARD_CAP + 10` aborts with 1ms steps → `pendingAborts.size <= HARD_CAP`, newest id survives (consume succeeds), oldest id evicted (consume fails). Also asserts the behavioural path via the same run-fn registration shape as the existing tests.

## Verification

- `bun test packages/test/src/test/util/WorkerServerBase.race.test.ts` — runs the three new tests plus the three pre-existing abort-before-call race tests (regression coverage).
- Type-check + lint on the two source files.

## Risks

- The 30s TTL must comfortably exceed worst-case message-port roundtrip latency between the main thread and the worker. In practice this is microseconds-to-milliseconds, so 30s is a 10,000x safety margin — not a concern.
- `consumePendingAbort` now rechecks `Date.now() - ts > TTL` on every call (one extra subtraction). Negligible.
- The per-id `setTimeout` adds one timer per abort. With the 10k hard cap that's at most 10k pending timers — well within Node/Bun limits, and they GC as they fire.

## Rollback

Two independent commits, each rollback-able on its own:
1. `fix(util/worker): TTL-based pendingAborts eviction` — revert restores the FIFO Set policy and removes the new tests.
2. `docs(ai/task): clarify runWithIterable abort bond is one-way` — comment-only; revert restores the prior JSDoc verbatim.

---

Note: this PR is branched off `main` as `claude/loving-mendel-Hcznj-abort` rather than the default session branch `claude/loving-mendel-Hcznj` because a separate PR re-enabling CI is being authored on that branch in parallel. The two changes have independent review concerns and should be reviewable in isolation.

author: pipiche38
body:
This branch documents the investigation and fixes for a memory growth issue observed during active runtime of the Domoticz-Zigbee plugin. The leak was identified using tracemalloc snapshots taken every 5 minutes, cross-referenced with new diagnostic stats added to DomoticzDB and ZigpyTransport.

1. CPython race condition in asyncio.wait_for + Semaphore.acquire() (primary cause)

On Python ≤ 3.11, asyncio.wait_for() wraps its awaitable in an internal Task. If the semaphore becomes available exactly when the timeout fires, the internal task can acquire the semaphore slot while wait_for still raises TimeoutError. The acquired flag stays False, so _limit_concurrency's finally block skips semaphore.release() — permanently consuming the slot. All subsequent tasks for that device then wait up to SEMAPHORE_TIMEOUT seconds before timing out, causing cascading task accumulation. Pre-fix growth measured at 6,852 asyncio tasks per 5 minutes; post-fix reduced to ~268 tasks per 5 minutes (25× reduction).

2. DomoticzDB circular reference and thread-safety issues

DomoticzAPIClient ↔ DomoticzDeviceCache formed a circular reference that prevented immediate garbage collection on plugin restart, relying on CPython's cyclic GC instead of reference counting. A missing lock on _device_caches allowed a race between the main thread and the worker thread.

- [x] Add hourly heartbeat calls to domoticz_api.dump_stats() and ControllerLink.dump_transport_stats() when their respective debug flags (DomoticzDB_Stats, ZigpyTransport_Stats) are enabled.
- [x] Add tracemalloc snapshot infrastructure: 5-minute lineno diffs for ongoing growth tracking, hourly filtered traceback diffs (excluding tracemalloc internal allocations) for call-chain identification. Controlled by the EnableTraceMalloc plugin config flag.
- [x] Fix crash in timeout_widget_api() Extended API path: _switch_off_widget_due_to_timedout() requires _nValue and _sValue arguments that were missing, which would raise TypeError whenever DOMOTICZ_EXTENDED_API is enabled and a device times out.
- [x] Break DomoticzAPIClient ↔ DomoticzDeviceCache circular reference on stop() by calling _device_caches.clear(), allowing immediate reference-counted collection on restart.
- [x] Add _device_caches_lock (threading.Lock) to protect _device_caches list from concurrent access between the main thread (registrations) and the worker thread (iteration).
- [x] Fix sentinel handling: replace continue with break so the worker loop exits immediately instead of rechecking _stop_event.
Guard update_device_from_response() against non-list payloads (e.g. gethardware responses) to prevent TypeError in the worker.
- [x] Add _prune_stale_devices() called after every full getdevices refresh to evict entries for devices deleted from Domoticz.
- [x] Add dump_stats() to both DomoticzAPIClient and DomoticzDeviceCache: logs cache size, inflight count, queue depth, device cache entry counts, entry ages, and approximate byte size. Called hourly via the plugin heartbeat.
- [x] Making sure to rebuild IEEE2NWK when loading from Domoticz
- [x] storing on Domoticz V2
        - v1 (existing): b64→not-compressed→Python-repr → survives because zlib fails gracefully and ast.literal_eval is still the fallback.
       - v2 (new writes): b64→zlib→JSON → clean path
- [x] Code refactoring of packet_received() 
       - Bug fixed
         - The 0x8034 branch was logging "0x8036" — now fixed to "0x8034 (Mgmt_Leave_rsp)".
       - Behavioural change fixed
         The original ZDO/coordinator branch called super() but then fell through to the rest of the method, building an unnecessary 8002 frame.  One side-effect worth being aware of: for a ZDO packet that is not 0x8036/0x8034 and not profile 0x0104, super().packet_received() ends up being called twice — once in the ZDO branch, and again at step 5b. 
      - Structural improvements
         - _unpack_packet() isolates all the int(... if ... else None) unpacking in one place, keeping the main method clean.
         - _handle_zdo_cluster() merges the two nearly-identical cluster branches (0x8036 / 0x8034) into a single helper that returns True when it matched, so the caller can return cleanly.
         - Named constants (CLUSTER_MGMT_PERMIT_JOIN_RSP, PROFILE_ZHA, etc.) replace all magic numbers.
         - _pkt_summary() eliminates the repeated sender / profile / cluster / srcEp / dstEp / message format string.
         - Section comments (# ── 1. …) make the routing steps scannable without reading every line.
         - packet.lqi = packet.lqi or 0x00 replaces the verbose if … is None pattern.

**Enable the new diagnostic flags in the plugin configuration via WebUI settings -Experimental parameters**:

- DomoticzDB_Stats = true
- ZigpyTransport_Stats = true
- EnableTraceMalloc = true

Then monitor the plugin log. Under normal operation you should see:

DomoticzDB stats | cache=N/16 | inflight=0 | queue≈0 — all bounded
ZigpyTransport stats | asyncio_tasks=N (pending=N) — tasks drain to single digits during quiet periods
Freed: -X KB lines in tracemalloc output confirming GC is reclaiming send-task memory between bursts

author: jasonmmo
body:
## Summary

eGov boot scaffolds crash on startup (egov5-boot-jdk17-jakarta) because the
log4jdbc DriverSpy wrapper turns an HSQLDB `SQLFeatureNotSupportedException`
into a fatal HikariCP pool-init error.

Trace (reproduced with HikariCP 6.3.3 + HSQLDB 2.7.4 + log4jdbc-log4j2 1.16):

```
java.sql.SQLFeatureNotSupportedException: feature not supported
  at org.hsqldb.jdbc.JDBCConnection.setNetworkTimeout(Unknown Source)
  at net.sf.log4jdbc.sql.jdbcapi.ConnectionSpy.setNetworkTimeout(ConnectionSpy.java:1120)
  at com.zaxxer.hikari.pool.PoolBase.getAndSetNetworkTimeout(PoolBase.java:549)
  at com.zaxxer.hikari.pool.PoolBase.setupConnection(PoolBase.java:417)
  at com.zaxxer.hikari.pool.HikariPool.createPoolEntry(HikariPool.java:488)
```

`boot-jdk17-jakarta` works because it wires HikariCP directly to
`org.hsqldb.jdbc.JDBCDriver`. This PR copies that pattern into both
eGov boot runners (`application.yml` + `EgovConfigAppDatasource`).

## Changes

- `egov5-boot-jdk17-jakarta`: drop log4jdbc DriverSpy from `application.yml`
  and `EgovConfigAppDatasource.java`; javadoc the root cause.
- `egov4-boot-jdk8-javax`: same change for symmetry. HikariCP 4.x bundled
  with Spring Boot 2.7 swallows the exception today, but keeping both
  runners aligned prevents drift when the lane is upgraded.

## Test plan

- [x] `mvn spring-boot:run` on a freshly scaffolded egov5 project boots
      without HikariPool init failure.
- [ ] Smoke `POST /uiadapter/select_datalist.do` returns nexacro envelope.
- [ ] Smoke `POST /uiadapter/sampleLargeData.do` streams without truncation.

## Notes

Pom-level `log4jdbc-log4j2-jdbc4.1` dependency and
`log4jdbc.log4j2.properties` are left untouched to keep this PR minimal.
They are unused after this change but harmless; a follow-up can prune
them if desired.

## Done

  - **Per-request CSP nonce wired up in `webapp/handlers.py`.** Lazily generates a ~128-bit base64-urlsafe nonce on `flask.g`, exposes it to all templates as `csp_nonce`, and
   appends `'nonce-XYZ'` to `script-src`, `script-src-elem`, and `style-src` when building the response header. Lazy generation (vs. a `before_request` hook) is intentional —

The catch-all `* @hyperpolymath` line in CODEOWNERS causes GitHub to auto-request review on every Dependabot PR (since every PR touches at least one owned path under `*`). With the sole maintainer being the same user, those review requests are pure notification noise.

This drops the wildcard line while preserving any path-specific ownership and SPDX/license headers. Path-specific lines are intentional and stay.

Human PRs from collaborators still trigger path-owner review where applicable; Dependabot PRs typically only touch root manifest files which are no longer matched.

body:
This PR updates the repository's .gitignore configuration to ensure that local development environments remain secure and clean. It establishes comprehensive exclusion rules to prevent IDE-specific files, build artifacts, and sensitive local configurations from being inadvertently committed to version control.
Changes Included:
•
Local Properties & Secrets: Explicitly ignores local.properties (used for backend configuration), along with common keystore formats (*.keystore, *.jks, *.pem, *.p12) and .env files.
•
IDE Configuration: Ignores IDE-specific directories (.idea/, .vscode/) and system files (e.g., .DS_Store).
•
Build Artifacts: Ensures all generated build directories (/build/, /app/build/), Gradle caches, and Android compilation artifacts (*.apk, *.aab) are excluded.
Testing Instructions:
•
Run git status locally to verify that your personal local.properties, keystores, and IDE configuration folders are no longer tracked as untracked files by Git.
